newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures close sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures close sharply lower.

text.p: Renewed selling linked to further weakness in cash lumber prices offset early short covering and CME lumber futures tumbled to sharply lower closes, traders said.
Lumber closed mostly $7.00 to $2.20 per thousand board foot lower, paced by March at $393.50 and May off $2.20 at $377.30 per tbf.

Carryover support from Tuesday's late recovery gave way to renewed general selling sparked by the continued cash weakness. The market was also technically weak and a close under $395 in March was viewed as technically very bearish, they said.

Random Lengths quoted cash spruce Wednesday at $404 per tbf, down $10 from Friday and $12 under a week ago. But wholesalers continued to offer wood under the mill level to move product, cash sources said.
"It looks like we're going to need some kind of wash out in cash to clean things up," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst.
Schmadick estimated that wholesalers are offering spruce in the $380 to $390 per tbf area.
